chunk_findings.detail: The guard only ever records and compares `_config_snapshot()` (locals from `.git/config` + `core.bare`) and `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no`; it never records `HEAD` or the branch ref. That is exactly the state a stray commit mutates, so the guard can stay silent while the item's branch is polluted with "Test init" commits — the headline symptom of B1d82c6b76f. Concrete input: a test that runs `git -C tmp add README.md && git -C tmp commit -m 'Test init'` while `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` still point at the real repository (i.e., any future regression of the leak this file guards against), supplying the identity with `-c user.name=… -c user.email=…` so `.git/config` is never written, and staging content that matches the work tree. After the run: `.git/config` is byte-identical to `_BASELINE` (no `user.name`, no `core.bare` change), `git status --porcelain` is identical to the baseline (clean), yet `git rev-parse HEAD` moved and `git log` shows the extra commit. `_changes(_BASELINE, snapshot(status=False))` in the module fixture and `_changes(_BASELINE, snapshot())` in `pytest_sessionfinish` both find nothing, so the suite exits 0 while the branch was rewritten — the opposite of the guarantee the guard is documented to give. (Note the per-module fixture passes `status=False` and therefore also cannot attribute tracked-file/index changes to a module; only `pytest_sessionfinish` sees them, and neither path sees refs.)
chunk_findings.title: tests/_isolation.py `snapshot` / `pytest_sessionfinish` (and the `_real_repo_config_untouched` fixture)

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_local_identity_equal_to_the_global_one_is_not_a_finding` unconditionally reads the machine's *global* git identity via `_git(repo, "config", "--global", f"user.{key}")`, and `_git` runs `subprocess.run(..., check=True)`. When no global identity is configured (the normal state of a fresh CI container / isolated test runner — exactly the environment this bug is about, `pytest -n 48` under `ddflow gate run <id> ci`), `git config --global user.name` exits 1, so `subprocess.run` raises `CalledProcessError` and the test errors before exercising the code under review. The change has no setup that guarantees a global identity exists (no `git config --global …` write, no `HOME`/`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` isolation that would make one), it just assumes the developer's global config is present. The same assumption underlies the identity comparison: with no global value, the identity the `repo` fixture must configure locally to be able to commit will read as "local identity unlike the global one", so `test_a_clean_repository_has_no_hygiene_note` (line 29) also diverges. Either way the suite outcome depends on the runner's `[REDACTED:path]` rather than on the change.

chunk_findings.detail:
`_get` returns the empty string both when the config key is genuinely unset **and** when `git config` cannot run, so a *failure to answer* is indistinguishable from "no global identity". In `identity_notes`, `shared = _global(repo, "user.name")` therefore yields `""` whenever `git config --global …` fails, which takes the `else "(no global one)"` branch and emits:

> the repository config sets user.name = 'X' (no global one): every commit and merge from every worktree carries it. If nobody set it on purpose (a test or script run in the wrong directory does), `git -C <primary> config --local --unset user.name`.

Concretely: run `ddflow doctor` from a process whose environment has no `HOME` (`env -u HOME ddflow doctor`, or a cron/systemd/CI unit with a scrubbed environment). `git -C repo config --global --get user.name` then exits 128 with `fatal: $HOME not set`, `r.ok` is False and `_get` returns `""`, while `git config --local` (which does not need `HOME`) still returns the repo's legitimate `user.name`. The note fires and advises unsetting a deliberate identity — after which commits fail with "please tell me who you are". This directly contradicts the module docstring's promise that "Git unable to answer is silence here, never a claim", which the other two checks honor (`bare_notes`/`stale_primary_notes` guard on `r.ok` before claiming anything); `identity_notes` needs to distinguish the unset case from the failed-read case before treating the global value as absent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/repo_hygiene.py:40 (`_get`) / `identity_notes` (line ~55)

chunk_findings.detail: The guard silently misses a stray commit on the real repository whenever the commit subject is not exactly `"init"` or `"Test init"`. `_changes` iterates the snapshot keys but explicitly skips `"head"` (`if key != "head" and ...`), and the only HEAD check is `stray_commits`, which filters `git log <since>..<head>` through the hard-coded `STRAY_SUBJECTS` allow-list. Concretely: a fixture that runs `subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-m", "add fixture"], cwd=<path that turns out to be the real repo>)` (the exact class of bug B1d82c6b76f describes: "a test runs git commit in the current directory instead of its tmp repo") commits with the identity supplied by the new scratch `GLOBAL_CONFIG` (`name = Test`), so the real repo's `.git/config` and `core.bare` are unchanged; the commit consumes the change, so `git status --porcelain -uno` is clean; the only difference between `_BASELINE` and the later `snapshot()` is `head`, which is never compared and whose new commits do not match `STRAY_SUBJECTS`. `_changes` therefore returns `[]`, the module fixture and `pytest_sessionfinish` both pass, and the item's branch keeps a stray commit — while the guard reports success. Note this is made *more* likely by this very change: the scratch `[user]` identity lets a test commit without writing any per-repo config, which is precisely the case that leaves the config/status checks green. Comparing `head` directly (any HEAD movement) instead of inferring it from a subject allow-list, or dropping the subject filter, would close it.
chunk_findings.title: tests/_isolation.py:`_changes` / `stray_commits`

chunk_findings.detail:
The test hard-codes `refs/heads/main` to make the primary checkout stale (`_git(repo, "update-ref", "refs/heads/main", "feat")`, with the comment "main moved, the primary did not follow"), but nothing in this file (or the autouse `_global_identity` fixture, which only writes `[user]`) establishes that the fixture repo's checked-out branch is `main`. On any host where `git init` still defaults to `master` (or where the project configures another default), the fixture repo is on `master`; the `update-ref` merely creates a new, unchecked-out `refs/heads/main` pointing at the `feat` commit, while `HEAD` keeps following `master`, whose tree and index still agree with the primary work tree. `RH.doctor_notes(repo)` then yields an empty list, so `[note] = RH.doctor_notes(repo)` raises `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 1, got 0)` — the test fails for an environment reason, not a code reason. The current branch should be obtained from the fixture (e.g. `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD`) instead of assumed to be `main`.

Note: on the intended path (repo on `main`) the rest of the assertions are consistent; the environment-dependence above is the concrete failure mode I can demonstrate from the diff.

chunk_findings.detail: This change modifies `repo_hygiene.check_identity` — `_get`/`_global` may now return `None`, and the caller silently `continue`s ("no claim") — and in the same diff it **deletes the only test that exercises that path**. With the test present, `repo` had `user.name='Stray'` while the scratch global config carried `Test`, and the assertion `any("user.name = 'Stray'" in n for n in _notes(repo))` was the one thing requiring the doctor to actually emit the local/global mismatch note. After deletion, a regression in exactly the edited code (e.g. `_global` returning `None` for every probe, so every mismatch is skipped) would pass the whole suite unnoticed. There is also a root-cause concern: the bug being fixed is that a test ran `git commit`/`ddflow init` in the process cwd and left `init` commits on the item branch; `run_cli(repo, "init")` in this deleted test is the kind of call that produces such commits. Removing the caller removes the reproduction instead of making that command run in the tmp repo, so the underlying defect (a git command using cwd rather than the fixture repo) remains reachable from any other `ddflow init` invocation, and the fix ships without the regression coverage the hard constraint requires [D-rules-hierarchy].
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_repo_hygiene_doctor.py `test_ddflow_doctor_reports_the_hygiene_notes`

chunk_findings.detail: The "a real change" commit is made with only `-c user.email=[REDACTED:email]`, leaving the author (and committer) name at the fixture repo's suite identity (`Test`). The bug being regression-tested is that fixture commits are recognized by exactly that identity `Test <…>`, and the repro inspects `%an`. The later legit commit at line 151 is careful to supply a complete identity (`Op <[REDACTED:email]>`), which only makes sense if the suite identity includes the name. Given that, `ISO.stray_commits(base)` at line 141 does not return `[]`: it returns the "a real change" commit, so `assert ISO.stray_commits(base) == []` fails (and the `[stray] = ISO.stray_commits(base)` unpacking at line 144 would raise `ValueError` too). The override needs to set `user.name` as well (or use `--author "Op <[REDACTED:email]>"`, as the final commit does); overriding the email alone is insufficient whenever the detector compares the author name or the full `name <email>` pair.

chunk_findings.detail: This change deletes `test_ddflow_doctor_reports_the_hygiene_notes` outright — the diff shows the whole function removed and no replacement added anywhere else. Before this change, that test was the only place that exercised the CLI path end‑to‑end: it ran `run_cli(repo, "init")`, set a divergent local identity (`git config user.name Stray`), and asserted `_notes(repo)` contained `user.name = 'Stray'`. The only remaining test in this file, `test_a_local_identity_equal_to_the_global_one_is_not_a_finding`, calls `RH.doctor_notes(repo)` directly, so it covers the service function but not the `ddflow doctor`/CLI wiring that surfaces those notes. After this diff, a regression that stops the CLI from reporting a hygiene note (or drops the note in the CLI layer while `repo_hygiene` still returns it) would pass the whole suite. The new test added in `tests/test_test_isolation.py` is about `ISO.stray_commits`/`_changes`, not about the doctor CLI, so it does not replace this coverage. The deleted test is still valid under the new autouse `_global_identity` fixture (global `Test`, local `Stray` is exactly the divergent case it asserts), so its removal is not forced by the fixture change and leaves a real gap in the regression protection for the area being fixed.

chunk_findings.detail: The guard only ever records and compares `_config_snapshot()` (locals from `.git/config` + `core.bare`) and `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no`; it never records `HEAD` or the branch ref. That is exactly the state a stray commit mutates, so the guard can stay silent while the item's branch is polluted with "Test init" commits — the headline symptom of B1d82c6b76f. Concrete input: a test that runs `git -C tmp add README.md && git -C tmp commit -m 'Test init'` while `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` still point at the real repository (i.e., any future regression of the leak this file guards against), supplying the identity with `-c user.name=… -c user.email=…` so `.git/config` is never written, and staging content that matches the work tree. After the run: `.git/config` is byte-identical to `_BASELINE` (no `user.name`, no `core.bare` change), `git status --porcelain` is identical to the baseline (clean), yet `git rev-parse HEAD` moved and `git log` shows the extra commit. `_changes(_BASELINE, snapshot(status=False))` in the module fixture and `_changes(_BASELINE, snapshot())` in `pytest_sessionfinish` both find nothing, so the suite exits 0 while the branch was rewritten — the opposite of the guarantee the guard is documented to give. (Note the per-module fixture passes `status=False` and therefore also cannot attribute tracked-file/index changes to a module; only `pytest_sessionfinish` sees them, and neither path sees refs.)
chunk_findings.title: tests/_isolation.py `snapshot` / `pytest_sessionfinish` (and the `_real_repo_config_untouched` fixture)

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_local_identity_equal_to_the_global_one_is_not_a_finding` unconditionally reads the machine's *global* git identity via `_git(repo, "config", "--global", f"user.{key}")`, and `_git` runs `subprocess.run(..., check=True)`. When no global identity is configured (the normal state of a fresh CI container / isolated test runner — exactly the environment this bug is about, `pytest -n 48` under `ddflow gate run <id> ci`), `git config --global user.name` exits 1, so `subprocess.run` raises `CalledProcessError` and the test errors before exercising the code under review. The change has no setup that guarantees a global identity exists (no `git config --global …` write, no `HOME`/`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` isolation that would make one), it just assumes the developer's global config is present. The same assumption underlies the identity comparison: with no global value, the identity the `repo` fixture must configure locally to be able to commit will read as "local identity unlike the global one", so `test_a_clean_repository_has_no_hygiene_note` (line 29) also diverges. Either way the suite outcome depends on the runner's `[REDACTED:path]` rather than on the change.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_repo_hygiene_doctor.py:45

chunk_findings.detail: This change deletes `test_ddflow_doctor_reports_the_hygiene_notes` outright — the diff shows the whole function removed and no replacement added anywhere else. Before this change, that test was the only place that exercised the CLI path end‑to‑end: it ran `run_cli(repo, "init")`, set a divergent local identity (`git config user.name Stray`), and asserted `_notes(repo)` contained `user.name = 'Stray'`. The only remaining test in this file, `test_a_local_identity_equal_to_the_global_one_is_not_a_finding`, calls `RH.doctor_notes(repo)` directly, so it covers the service function but not the `ddflow doctor`/CLI wiring that surfaces those notes. After this diff, a regression that stops the CLI from reporting a hygiene note (or drops the note in the CLI layer while `repo_hygiene` still returns it) would pass the whole suite. The new test added in `tests/test_test_isolation.py` is about `ISO.stray_commits`/`_changes`, not about the doctor CLI, so it does not replace this coverage. The deleted test is still valid under the new autouse `_global_identity` fixture (global `Test`, local `Stray` is exactly the divergent case it asserts), so its removal is not forced by the fixture change and leaves a real gap in the regression protection for the area being fixed.
